name: the header-background fallback goes back to the stale literal
why: org/config-handling.org F4, reverted at the site a person actually sees: the CSS block's `Lib.settings.sa_ui_thead_th_bg || '#e8e8e8'` against a schema default of '#bababa'. With the colour field cleared, the header renders the literal instead of the default. Only the CLEARED test may notice — the unset-setting control must stay green, because that path never reaches the `||`.
grep: a CLEARED colour falls back to the schema default

name: the filter-row fallback goes back to the stale literal
why: The second colour the same test pins, mutated separately so each is its own guard rather than one assertion covering for the other. Same shape: '#f4f4f4' inline against a '#d1d1d1' default.
grep: a CLEARED colour falls back to the schema default

name: the setting stops being read at all, and the colour is hardcoded
why: The plausible wrong fix: 'make the header #bababa' taken to mean hardcoding it. The two cleared/unset tests would BOTH still pass, because #bababa is what they expect — only the counter-guard, which sets a colour of its own, can see it. That is why that third test exists.
grep: a colour the user actually chose still wins

name: the unset-setting control, under the header mutation
why: EXPECTED TO PASS, and recorded because the pass is the point. Reverting the inline literal cannot change what an UNSET setting renders: `settingsInterface.init()` has already put the schema default into Lib.settings, so the `||` never fires. This pins the claim the spec's header comment makes about when the fallback is live — if this ever starts failing, that reasoning is wrong and the whole framing of F4 needs revisiting.
grep: an unset setting already rendered the schema default
